cards.note: Already npm-package shaped: package.json declares dsh.bundle.patch and the cordis.patch.yml insert row is the install path; no dsh.plugin.json and no repository-plugin artifacts remain, so the removed mechanism is not used.
Manifest carries dsh.client (platform web + ./client export) and no legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json.
The client half declares dsh.client and exports ./client, so the client-modules scan sees it; the bundle artifact format itself is the separate build-preset gap.

Every consumed service is declared: inject = ['tools','webServer']; settings and connection are claimed through ctx.inject([...]) bridges, never by undeclared ctx.get or property access (client half: inject = ['slots','locale','connection']).

Optional host services degrade instead of widening inject: ctx.inject(['settings']) keeps the documented no-provider fallback, and the custom route lives inside ctx.inject(['connection']) so it fails closed when the gate is absent.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state, so the event discriminator and turn/end semantics never arise.
The browser half is a settings card; it consumes no ctx.sessions or client runtime session API and aggregates no session mood.
The plugin tails no task/run output; there is no tasks.peek consumer to rebuild on tasks.read plus a shadow buffer.

Already on the 0812 names: inject uses webServer and the gateway registers through ctx.webServer.register (kind 'prefix'); no tasks/onTaskDone usage exists. Verified against packages/host/webserver at the target tag.
No image attachment refs, read_image use, or persisted image metadata in the plugin.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses, nor snapshot-tests read_image.
No LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache: the plugin registers interpreter tools and a settings surface only.
No APIProxy call site: the host half talks to services (tools, settings, webServer, connection) and its own HTTP route; it imports no host-internal client package.
The plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents, so the alpha.1 ignorable removal and the alpha.2 restore do not touch it.
No host source patches and no internal session-view imports; the plugin uses public services and its own route only.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration, or direct profile-file reading; the plugin ships a bundle patch row only.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser in the plugin.
The plugin registers ordinary tools and uses no tool presentation mode, PTC preset, dispatch waterfall, or related type.
Not a permission, approval, WebFetch policy, or audit plugin; no web_fetch policy is shipped or consumed.

The documented self-hosted route is kept and now runs behind the Connection gate: the handler calls ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) and answers 401/403 before touching settings; registration lives in ctx.inject(['connection']) so the route never exists ungated. Browser fetches ride the token-exchanged cookie.
Not a model provider plugin; the optional provider-login settings capability is unused.
Card copy uses the official ctx.locale.register API for the plugin's own zh/en dictionaries; the plugin carries no custom i18n patch and registers no third-party language.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface in the plugin.
Informational privacy/deployment surface: the official adapter may attach plugin package metadata, which needs no plugin code change (deployments decide per policy).
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker compatibility workarounds are maintained.
The plugin does not use the official DeepSeek LLM API and does not consider enabling session-log-deepseek.

The acceptance record opens the token launch URL (cookie exchange), then reads window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries, finds the plugin entry by package name, and requests the advertised client artifact; the route spec asserts the 401 without the session cookie.
No structured-question answerer registration; the plugin registers no user-questions provider.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions and no agent-presets roots configured by the plugin.
No stream-chunk handling or TPS computation; the card consumes committed config values, not token deltas.
The plugin's bundle patch inserts its own row only; it does not reuse the dsh-base composition or restate telemetry rows, so no privacy-stance override is owned here.
No dependency on @earendil-works/pi-ai or on dsh-llm-pi-ai; no provider/auth plugin surface.

The removed dsh-client-runtime surface is rehomed: the card's SnapshotStore type comes from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store and the client context type from @deepseek-ai/cordis; dsh-client-runtime is absent from dsh.client.inject and from peers.

All the ids agree on package.json#name: the hand-rolled lazy-CJS bundle registers as @bench/dsh-bench-interpreters-card via window.__ModuleLoader__.load, exports the same name, and the cordis.patch.yml row uses the bare package name.
The card reads the plugin's own /interpreters/api route; it reads no session timeline, user message content, or SessionBinding event window.
No composer DOM manipulation: the card owns settings inputs, not draft injection, history recall, or selection operations.
The card renders no MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock from ui-primitives, so the nested labels shape never arises.
No ctx.connection.api consumption: the client half injects connection only for the connection/reset invalidation event.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors or subagent/descriptor event consumers.
No IWorkspaces navigation or directory-picker calls; the card has no workspace surface.
The plugin writes no third-party persisted SessionEvents, so the ignorable restore has no producer to mark.
No ctx.remote unary calls or Remote failure handling in either half.

Peer graph recomposed for this release: dsh-client-runtime and dsh-client-ui-settings removed, dsh-host-webserver and dsh-client-ui-renderer restored/added, all DSH peers floored at ^0.1.2-alpha.2, cordis at ^4.0.1; the host half's runtime library @deepseek-ai/schemastery moved from the optional-peer block to dependencies so an install provides it (the repo carries no lockfile).
No startup wrapper or CI matrix in the plugin, so no Node 24.0-24.11.1 workaround exists to remove.
The card consumes no pluginInventory/list snapshot and validates no PluginInventorySnapshot.
No host.describe call and no ctx.remote.$host usage; the only Host fact the card needs is the config it fetches through its own route.

The plugin is a leaf bundle plugin, not a self-composed profile mounting dsh-tool-todo / dsh-tool-subagent / dsh-agent / dsh-agent-loop individually; it declares none of those as peers, so no sessionProjections row is owned here.
The namespace is a literal constant (INTERPRETERS_NS) passed directly to installSection and settings.update; the removed runtime settingsNamespace helper is not imported anywhere.
